rationale: Lycopolitan variant of ⲧϣⲱⲃⲉ 'exchange, change' (Sahidic ϣⲓⲃⲉ). In the speech-as-coin parable of this kephalaion, names the verbal exchange / responsive interaction between speakers, paralleling the monetary exchange of the coin-currency.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲗⲁⲥ 'tongue' (vowel-shift ⲁ→ⲉ). Standard speech-organ in the mouth-anatomy sequence (tongue → teeth → lips) describing speech production.
Lycopolitan variant of ⲛⲁϫϩⲉ 'teeth' with ⲭ for ϫ. Distinct register from accumulated ⲛⲁⲃⲍⲉ 'teeth' (King-of-Darkness body-schema); this form belongs to the speech-anatomy register.
Lycopolitan variant of ⲛ̄ⲥⲡⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'their lips' (cf. ⲥⲟⲁⲡⲉⲧ in glossary), or ⲛ̄-ⲥⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩ. The third member of the speech-organ chain in this kephalaion.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ϭⲟⲙ 'power, might,' with ⲧ for ϭ. Used here for the power of the five members through which the word comes forth.
Greek loanword νόμισμα 'coin, currency.' Central technical term of this kephalaion's parable: the word is fashioned by five faculties as a coin is fashioned by five artisans.
Lycopolitan reflex of an inscribing/engraving stem (possibly ⲟⲩⲱⲧϩ̄ extended). The coin-fashioning verbal series describes successive stages of the minting process. Tentative.
Reduplicated intensive of a Lycopolitan stem ⲭⲱⲍ (= ϫⲱϩ, perhaps cognate with ϫⲱⲱϫⲉ 'engrave'). Reduplication suggests intensive/iterative striking of the engraving tool.
Adverbial phrase ⲉ- + ϩⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'circuit, round' (cf. ⲡⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'encompassing circuit' in glossary). Describes cutting the coin-blank to a round shape.

proposed_english: the body of the blank / the metal blank
rationale: Compound apparently incorporating ⲙⲉϣ- (a weighing/measuring or kneading element) + ⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'body.' In the coin-parable register, names the unstamped metal flan (planchet) that receives the strike. Tentative.
Lycopolitan verb of striking/forging the metal blank. Possibly cognate with ⲡⲱⲧϣ̄/ⲡⲁϩⲧ̄ 'cast down, strike.' Coin-minting register.
Greek loanword τεχνίτης 'craftsman, artisan.' The five artisans = the five faculties (cf. accumulated ⲧⲉⲭⲛⲏⲧⲏⲥ in same sense).
Greek loanword χρῆμα 'thing, money, currency.' Lycopolitan orthography ⲭⲣⲓⲙⲁ for χρῆμα. Names the function of the minted coin as monetary medium.

Lycopolitan variant of ⲃⲝⲃⲓⲗⲉ in glossary (with metathesis ⲗ↔ⲝ). 'Grain, kernel, particle' — small agricultural unit. ⲧⲃⲗⲃⲓⲗⲉ ⲛⲥⲟⲩⲟ 'grain of wheat,' ⲧⲃⲗⲃⲓⲗⲉ ⲛⲓⲱⲧ 'grain of barley.' Central image of this kephalaion.
Standard Coptic ⲥⲟⲩⲟ 'wheat' (cf. Sahidic ⲥⲟⲩⲟ). The grain-of-wheat in the agricultural parable.
Coptic ⲉⲓⲱⲧ 'barley' (Crum 86b) — distinct from homograph ⲉⲓⲱⲧ 'father.' Confirmed by collocation +ⲃⲗⲃⲓⲗⲉ ⲛⲥⲟⲩⲟ ⲙⲛ̄ +ⲃⲗⲃⲓⲗⲉ ⲛⲓⲱⲧ 'grain of wheat and grain of barley' — the agricultural-cereal pair.

Tentatively a Lycopolitan verb of warming/heating from the stem ϩⲙⲟⲙ/ⲍⲙⲁⲙ 'be hot.' Functions as the verbal correlate of ⲡⲍⲙⲁⲙ 'the heat' in the elemental-dyad construction with ⲡⲁⲣⲁϣ 'cold.' Confidence low — alternative readings as adverbial state or different lexeme remain possible.

Verbal compound ⲣ̄- + ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'do-light,' standard Coptic for 'give light, illumine.' Used here of the chosen ones in the agricultural-correspondential register: just as the grain ripens and gives nourishment, so the chosen ones illumine.

Hapax in this corpus, appearing in line 25 amid heavy damage (abgerieben). Possible Lyc. reflex of ϩⲱⲃ 'work, yoke' or related abundance/satiety term that would pair antithetically with ⲍⲕⲟ 'hunger' in line 26. Confidence very low.
Greek loanword δικαιοσύνη with characteristic Lycopolitan orthography: ⲇ→ zero, ⲓⲕⲁⲓ→ⲁⲓⲕⲩⲁⲓ. The parable-application term naming the moral-soteriological correlate of the new-grain typology.
